Four things in that output repay a second look.

**Three parties for a two-party call.** The last entry is sipnab.

- It carries no `sip` URI. sipnab sent no SIP, and a synthesized one would name a
  participant that never existed.
- Its `role` says `observer`.
- Both attachments point their `party` index at it (index 2).
  So every document in the container has a stated origin.

**The callee has fewer fields than the caller.** Party 1 carries a `sip` and
nothing else.

- sipnab reads a party's `Contact` and `User-Agent` off a message
  that party sent.
- In this capture, the first message coming back is a bare
  `100 Trying`. It carries neither.
- An absent field means the capture never saw
  one. It does not mean the endpoint has none.

**The Dialog Object describes no media, and that is correct here.**

- This run retained no RTP payload. So there is nothing to describe.
- Inventing a `mediatype` or a `url` would name a file that does not exist.
- The object's type is `recording` with no content. This is the placeholder of the type rule below.
- It has no `disposition`. The call in this fixture completed, and
  nothing about it failed.

**The completeness body appears twice.** It appears once as an attachment, and once inside the
report. The next section is about why.

## What the Dialog Object says about the call

The first Dialog Object describes the call's signaling.
sipnab fills these fields from what the capture shows, and leaves a field out when the capture does not show it.

- `parties` is `[0, 1]`: the `From` party, then the `To` party.
  - [Section 4.3.4 of draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.3.4) makes `parties` a SHOULD on a `recording` and optional on an `incomplete`.
  - On an `incomplete` object it names the two parties the call tried to connect.
  - A container that carries audio lists the parties per channel instead, and only when sipnab can attribute every channel.
- `originator` is absent when party 0 is the caller.
  - [Section 4.3.5](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.3.5) writes it only when the first listed party is not the originator.
  - Party 0 is the caller when the capture holds the request that created the dialog, which carries no `To` tag.
  - When the capture joined the call later, the caller is not known.
    sipnab then adds an empty party, which carries only `validation`, before the observer, and `originator` names it.
    Section 4.3.5 gives that form for an originator that is not known.
- `duration` is the conversation in seconds, from the 200 to the initial INVITE to the BYE.
  - [Section 4.3.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.3.3) defines `duration` in seconds.
  - It is absent when the capture lacks the initial INVITE, its 200 or the BYE.
  - `start` stays the first message sipnab saw, so `start` plus `duration` is not the end of the call.
  - On an object with no `body` or `url`, `duration` is not the length of any recording.
    A consumer that reads `duration` to size media must check for content first.

- `sip_cseq` is the CSeq number of the request that created the dialog.
  - [Section 5.4 of draft-howe-vcon-sip-signaling-00](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-howe-vcon-sip-signaling-00#section-5.4) defines it as "the sequence number from the CSeq header field of the INVITE or other dialog-creating request".
  - It is absent when the capture joined after that request.

- `party_history` lists what the capture shows each party doing, in time order, per [section 4.3.13](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.3.13).
  - Each entry has `party`, `time` and `event`.
  - `join`: both parties, at the 200 to the initial INVITE, when the capture holds that INVITE and its 200.
  - `drop`: the sender of the first BYE, at the BYE, and the other party at the 2xx that answers it.
  - `hold`: a re-INVITE or UPDATE whose audio is `sendonly` or `inactive` puts the other party on hold, at the request.
  - `unhold`: a later `sendrecv` offer from the same sender takes that party off hold.
    A `recvonly` offer changes nothing.
  - `keydown` and `keyup` carry the digit in `button`, and appear only from a rule with `dtmf_events = true`.
    - An INFO with `application/dtmf-relay` is a `keydown` at the INFO and a `keyup` after its stated `Duration`.
    - An [RFC 4733](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4733.html) telephone event is a `keyup` at its end packet and a `keydown` its duration before.
      The event belongs to the party whose own SDP advertised the sending socket.
      When no SDP advertised the sending socket, the party whose SDP advertised the destination socket received the event, and the other party of the two sent it.
      This is the same SDP endpoint that links the stream to its dialog.
    - The rule turns telephone-event decoding on for the run.
    - sipnab keeps at most 256 telephone events per RTP stream (`MAX_KEY_PRESSES` (256) in the source). It drops later ones.
  - sipnab writes no `mute` or `unmute`, because SIP carries no signal for either.
  - A message whose tags match neither party adds nothing.
    An event adds nothing when neither party advertised its sending socket and no single party advertised its destination socket, because then sipnab cannot name a party as the receiver.
  - `--redact` removes `keydown` and `keyup`, because a digit can be a PIN, and keeps the rest.
  - A container that holds several legs moves each entry's `party` with the rest of the party indices.

### Text a party sent

Each SIP MESSAGE ([RFC 3428](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3428.html)) that carries content becomes a Dialog Object of type `text`, per [section 4.3.1.3 of draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.3.1.3).
These objects come after every other Dialog Object, so they move no index.

- There is one per message, and a retransmission with the same sender and CSeq is the same message.
- `start` is when sipnab captured the message.
  Section 4.3.2 uses the send time when the typing time is not known.
- `parties` lists the sender first, then the other party, so the sender is the originator and `originator` stays absent.
  - It is absent when the message's tag names neither party.
- `mediatype` is the message's `Content-Type` as written, and the body is inline.
  - A UTF-8 body uses `encoding: "none"`; any other body is base64url.
- A MESSAGE with no body is not a text dialog, and neither is an `application/im-iscomposing+xml` typing indication ([RFC 3994](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3994.html)).
- `--redact` removes the body, `encoding` and `mediatype`, and keeps `start` and `parties`, as it does for a recording.
- sipnab does not parse MSRP, so text sent over an MSRP session has no text dialog.

### Contact-center labels

A rule can copy three SIP headers into the `campaign`, `skill` and `interaction_id` parameters of [draft-ietf-vcon-cc-extension-02 section 3.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-cc-extension-02#section-3.2).
sipnab declares the `CC` extension in `extensions` already.

```toml
[[vcon.rule]]
name                  = "queues"
when                  = "method == 'INVITE'"
dir                   = "/var/spool/sipnab-vcon/queues"
campaign_header       = "X-Campaign"
skill_header          = "X-Queue"
interaction_id_header = "X-Interaction-ID"
```

- Each value comes from the first message in the call that carries the header, matched without regard to case.
- A header the call never carried, or one with no value, leaves its parameter absent.
- The values go on the first Dialog Object, the signaling one.
- A key that is not a SIP header name, such as one holding a space or a colon, refuses the run.
- `--redact` turns `interaction_id` into a token, so two containers of one interaction still match, and sweeps `campaign` and `skill` as free text.
- The parameter is `interaction_id`, as section 3.2.3 spells it.
  vcon-lib's list of Dialog parameters spells it `interaction`, so a vcon-lib reader that filters on that list drops it.

## A SIPREC recording session

On a tap beside a session recording server (SRS), sipnab sees the recording session that a session recording client (SRC) opens, not the recorded call itself.
[RFC 7866 section 6.1.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7866.html#section-6.1.1) puts the SRC in the `From` header and the SRS in the `To` header.
The people on the recorded call appear only in the [RFC 7865](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7865.html) metadata, the `application/rs-metadata+xml` part that the SRC sends beside its SDP.

When the recording session's INVITE, or a later request from the SRC, carries metadata that names at least one participant, the container shows the recorded call.

- Parties 0 and 1 stay the `From` and `To` of the recording session.
  - The party that sent the metadata has `role: "recording-client"`, and the other one has `role: "recording-server"`.
  - The `role` parameter comes from the `CC` extension, which sipnab already uses for `"observer"`.
    The extension allows values other than the ones it lists.
- Each `<participant>` becomes one party, in metadata order, after parties 0 and 1 and before the observer.
  - `sip` is the `aor` of the participant's `<nameID>` when it is a `sip:` or `sips:` URI.
    `tel` is the `aor` when it is a `tel:` URI, or a global number in the user part of a SIP AOR, by the rule in [`tel`](#one-thing-sipnab-does-supply-narrowly-tel).
  - `name` is the `<name>` inside the `<nameID>`.
    [RFC 7865 section 6.5.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7865.html#section-6.5.1) defines the pair: "nameID - This attribute is a list of (Name, AoR) tuples."
    sipnab reads the first `aor` and the first `<name>`.
  - An AOR that is a host name or an IP address gives no `sip` or `tel`. RFC 7865 allows both forms.
  - `validation` is `"none"` and `role` is absent.
    The SRC asserted these identities, and sipnab cannot check them.
- The `sipnab-siprec-streams` attachment maps each recorded stream to the party that sends it:

  ```json
  { "streams": [
      { "label": "0", "stream_id": "1a2b3c4d", "party": 2 },
      { "label": "1", "stream_id": "2b3c4d5e", "party": 2 },
      { "label": "2", "stream_id": "3c4d5e6f", "party": 3 } ] }
  ```

  - The sender is the participant whose `<participantstreamassoc>` lists the stream under `<send>`.
    [RFC 7865 section 6.8.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7865.html#section-6.8.1): "The presence of this attribute indicates that a participant is contributing to a stream."
    A `<recv>` entry does not make a participant the sender.
  - `party` is absent on a stream that no `<send>` names.
  - A container that holds several legs moves each `party` with the rest of the party indices.
- When the container carries audio, the recording's `parties` names the participant on each channel.
  - Each stream has an `a=label` on the m-line of the SRC's SDP that carries it.
    [RFC 7866 section 7.1.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7866.html#section-7.1.1) requires the SRC to put an `a=label` ([RFC 4574](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4574.html)) on each media stream, to tie the recorded stream to the metadata.
  - The `<label>` in the metadata names that m-line.
    [RFC 7865 section 6.7.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7865.html#section-6.7.1): "The 'label' attribute within the 'stream' XML element references an SDP "a=label" attribute that identifies an m-line within the RS SDP."
  - sipnab matches the address and port that sent the RTP to the m-line that names them, then follows the label to the stream and the stream to its sender.
  - The labels come from the SDP in the same message as the metadata.
    [RFC 7866 section 7.1.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7866.html#section-7.1.1) limits a label's scope to "the SDP and metadata conveyed in the bodies of the SIP request or response that the label appeared in."
  - When a channel's address and port match no labeled m-line, the rule for an ordinary call applies, and `parties` is usually absent.
- The completeness note says that the dialog is a SIPREC recording session, and where the participants came from.

A recording session whose metadata names no participant keeps the container of an ordinary call: three parties, no roles and no stream map.
The completeness note then says the dialog is a SIPREC recording session and why the participants are missing.
sipnab treats a dialog as a recording session in this case when its opening INVITE has `Require: siprec` or a `Contact` with `+sip.src`.
The note names one of two causes:

- no message in the dialog carried an `rs-metadata` part that sipnab could read, or
- the metadata named no participant, which is what a malformed or truncated XML body gives.

`--redact` rewrites a participant's `sip`, `tel` and `name` as it rewrites every other party's.
The metadata XML itself leaves the container with the other message bodies (see [The message trace](#the-message-trace)).

A container whose content a deny header withheld carries no participants.
Its parties are the SRC, the SRS and the observer.

## The SIP signaling attachments

The `sip-signaling` extension of [draft-howe-vcon-sip-signaling-00](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-howe-vcon-sip-signaling-00) stores SIP in attachments.
sipnab declares the extension in `extensions`.

### The message trace

The `sip-message-trace` attachment holds every message sipnab kept for the dialog.
Its body follows the trace format of [section 6.2.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-howe-vcon-sip-signaling-00#section-6.2.1), and keeps sipnab's own fields beside it.

- `version` is the string `"1.0"`, the trace format version the draft defines.
  - Until this release it was the number `1`.
  - `schema_version` stays the number `1` for readers of sipnab's own shape.
- `call_id` and `sip_call_id` both hold the Call-ID.
- Each message carries the draft's fields.
  - `timestamp` is when sipnab captured it.
  - `direction` is `"received"` on every message.
    The draft defines it from the producer's side, and sipnab sent nothing.
  - `party` is the index of the party whose tag the message carries.
    It is absent when the tags match neither party, such as a `100 Trying` from a proxy.
  - A request carries `method`.
    A response carries `status_code` and `status_text` instead.
  - `headers` maps each header name to a list of its values, without the credential headers.
  - `body` is the message body when there is one.
    A body that is not UTF-8 is base64url text, with `body_encoding: "base64url"`.
- Under `--redact`, no message keeps `body` or `body_encoding`.
  - A body can be the conversation itself, such as the text of a SIP MESSAGE.
  - The SDP is still in `sdp`, which redaction rewrites like every other field.
- A container that holds several legs moves each message's `party` with the rest of the party indices.

### The INVITE and the final response

A rule with `sip_messages = true` attaches the two messages [section 8.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-howe-vcon-sip-signaling-00#section-8.1) asks of a minimal producer.

```toml
[[vcon.rule]]
name         = "with-wire-messages"
when         = "method == 'INVITE'"
dir          = "/var/spool/sipnab-vcon/wire"
sip_messages = true
```

- `sip-invite` is the initial INVITE, and `sip-response` is its final response.
  - Both use `mediatype: "message/sip"` and hold the message as captured, per [section 6.1.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-howe-vcon-sip-signaling-00#section-6.1.2).
  - The final response is the last 200 to 699 response to an INVITE without a `To` tag.
    After a `407` challenge, that is the answer to the INVITE sent again with credentials.
  - The INVITE is the one with that response's CSeq number.
  - With no final response in the capture, sipnab attaches the last initial INVITE alone.
- `sip-sdp` holds the SDP body of each of the two, with `mediatype: "application/sdp"`, per [section 6.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-howe-vcon-sip-signaling-00#section-6.3).
- Each attachment's `party` is the party whose tag the message carries.
  - It is the observer when the tag matches neither party, such as a proxy's own response.
  - `start` is when sipnab captured the message, and `dialog` is 0.
- The bytes lose every credential header line, such as `Proxy-Authorization`, as the trace does.
  - sipnab keeps the body byte for byte, so `Content-Length` still matches it.
- UTF-8 messages use `encoding: "none"`; others use `base64url`.
- The rule's inline budget, `max_inline_media_mib` or `--vcon-max-inline-media`, covers the attachments together.
  - An attachment that does not fit stays out.
    The `sipnab-capture-completeness` attachment names it, with its size, in `sip_messages_refused`.
- `--redact` removes all three kinds of attachment.
  - The bytes hold every identifier the trace holds, and redaction cannot rewrite them without changing the message they copy.
- sipnab's own `-I` reader takes the messages from the trace, and reads `message/sip` attachments only from a container without a trace.

### The network's STIR verdict

sipnab checks no PASSporT signature and fetches no certificate.
When the network has verified a call, it says so in a `verstat` parameter (ATIS-1000074) on `P-Asserted-Identity` or `From`.
sipnab copies that verdict into a `stir-verification-report` attachment, the report of [section 7.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-howe-vcon-sip-signaling-00#section-7.3).

- The report comes from the first INVITE without a `To` tag that carries `verstat`.
  - sipnab reads `P-Asserted-Identity` first, then `From`.
  - With no `verstat`, there is no report, even when the INVITE carries a PASSporT.
- `result` maps the `verstat` value onto the draft's values.
  - `TN-Validation-Passed` is `verified`.
  - `TN-Validation-Failed` is `failed`.
  - `No-TN-Validation` is `no-signature` when the INVITE carried no `Identity` header.
    When it carried one, `result` is absent, because the draft has no value for "not verified".
- `attestation`, `orig_tn` and `dest_tn` are the claims of the PASSporT in the same INVITE, when there is one.
- `timestamp` is when sipnab captured the INVITE, which is after the network verified it.
- `verifier` is absent, because the header does not name who verified.
- `reason` states that sipnab transcribed the value and verified nothing.
- `verstat` and `verstat_header` keep the value as written and the header it came from.
- `party` is 0, the caller, and `dialog` is 0.
- `--redact` removes `orig_tn` and `dest_tn`, as it removes the PASSporT from the party.

### Tags

Every container a `[[vcon.rule]]` writes carries a `tags` attachment.
Its body is a list of `"name:value"` strings, the shape vcon-lib's `Vcon.add_tag` writes and `Vcon.get_tag` reads.

- `rule:<name>` names the rule that wrote the container.
- `filter:<name>` names each [named filter](@/docs/filter-dsl.md#named-filters) the rule's `when` references by `@name` and the call matched on its own.
  - The names follow the order of their first appearance in `when`.
  - A call matches a filter when at least one of its legs does.
- `finding:<name>` names each detection of the signaling diagnosis the analysis reports, at most five (`MAX_FINDING_TAGS` (5) in the source).
  - The names are the field names of `signaling_diagnosis` in the analysis body, such as `final_failure` or `retransmissions`, in that object's order.
  - A container that holds several legs names each finding once.
- No value contains a colon.
  vcon-lib takes the text between the first colon and the next one as the value.
- `party` is the observer and `dialog` is 0.
- A container from `--export-vcon-when`, the REST API or MCP has no rule name and carries no `tags` attachment.
- A withheld container carries none.

## The container cannot say "this is an incomplete record", so sipnab says it twice

This is the point of the page.

sipnab's central discipline is reporting what it understood rather than what
the wire held.

- Its ranked problem list puts incompleteness findings *in* the
  list at `Severity::Blind`, above every call fault.
- So a capture that failed to decode or hit a retention cap can never render as clean.

**vCon has no field for that.** Not a weak one: none.

- The `type` enum admits five values and no others: `recording`, `recording-set`, `text`, `transfer`,
  `incomplete`.
- Four of the five promise content the object holds.
- The fifth names a call that "failed to be setup". That is a claim about the conversation rather
  than about the object.

So sipnab types the object by **what it carries**. It also uses the one outcome it
can observe, a final failure:
| The object holds | `type` | `disposition` |
|---|---|---|
| audio | `recording` | absent — it is an `incomplete` field |
| no content, no observed failure | `recording`, with no content | absent |
| no content, an observed final failure | `incomplete` | the reason, always |

The middle row is the placeholder of
[section 4.3 of the core draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.3).

- It is for a dialog the producer knows occurred but holds little or nothing from.
- Such a Dialog Object "contains only
  the type parameter". For a call that reached setup, its type is `recording`.
- [Section 4.3.8](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.3.8) waives `mediatype` when the content is
  absent.
- "No observed failure" covers:
  - an answered call,
  - a call whose final response the capture never saw,
  - a redirect.
- sipnab cannot tell from the wire whether the second reached setup. It does not report a failure it did
  not see.

Reaching for `incomplete` in that row is the mistake sipnab shipped until
0.5.128.

- It is not a matter of taste.
- It made every container for a call that answered assert a setup failure that never happened.

**Changed in this release, for draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04.**

- Until now, that row had no `type` at all. `draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-03` allowed "a
  Dialog Object with no parameters in it".
- `-04` removed that sentence. It requires `type` on every Dialog Object.
- So a container for a call with no media now carries `"type": "recording"` and no `body` or `url`.
- A consumer that selects `type == "recording"` and then reads the content must check that the
  content is there.
- Measured in the vcon-server conserver source at commit `8ffbfcf`:
  - The `deepgram_link` transcription link reads `dialog["url"]` with a
    bracket, and raises on such an object.
  - The `hugging_face_whisper` and `groq_whisper` links read `dialog["duration"]` the same way.
  - The type-free object raised in all four transcription links, `openai_transcribe` included,
    at `dialog["type"]`.

The last two rows move together.

- [Section 4.3.11 of the core draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.3.11) makes `disposition` a MUST
  on an incomplete object.
- No value in its closed set means "not observed".
- So one decision fixes both fields.
- `disposition` names a failure **only** when sipnab saw the final response that caused it.
- Its absence never means "the call succeeded".

sipnab maps the final response to a value of that closed set:

| Final response | `disposition` | What section 4.3.11 defines the value as |
|---|---|---|
| `486`, `600` | `busy` | the party was busy with another conversation |
| `503` | `congestion` | system load stopped the attempt from completing |
| `408`, `480`, and `487` after a CANCEL sipnab saw | `no-answer` | nobody answered or accepted the attempt |
| any other `4xx`, `5xx` or `6xx`, a `487` with no CANCEL in the capture included | `failed` | the attempt failed, the value for a reason sipnab does not know |

A caller who gives up while the call rings sends CANCEL.

- The call ends with `487 Request Terminated`.
- Nobody answered, so that call is `no-answer`.
- sipnab never writes `hung-up`. The section defines it for a call that
  connected and then ended before any conversation.
- An answered call is not an `incomplete` object. The section says
  `disposition` "SHOULD NOT be present for other dialog types".

The extension mechanism offers no repair either. An extension is one of two kinds:

- *ignorable*: the consumer that most needs the caveat drops it,
- *fatal*: an ordinary consumer refuses the whole container.

Nothing in between means "read this before trusting the contents".

So sipnab duplicates the caveat into two surfaces a consumer walks past. Both come from
one source value:

| Surface | Where it sits | Who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| `capture_completeness`, inside `analysis[0].body` | inside the report, beside the diagnosis | anything that reads what sipnab concluded |
| the `sipnab-capture-completeness` attachment | a document in `attachments`, attributed to the observer | anything that walks the attachments |

Both hold the same value byte for byte. A test fails if they diverge.

- Two caveats that disagreed would read as authoritative while contradicting
  themselves.
- That is worse than carrying none.

### What the caveat looks like when the run lost something

This is the same capture and the same dialog. The run's parser rejected three frames. Its
idle compaction discarded four messages it had already captured:

```json
{
  "purpose": "sipnab-capture-completeness",
  "party": 2,
  "mediatype": "application/json",
  "encoding": "json",
  "body": {
    "dialogs_refused": 0,
    "dialogs_rotated": 0,
    "frames_read": 22,
    "messages_evicted": 4,
    "node": "capture-01",
    "note": "Produced by sipnab 0.5.127 on node capture-01. … sipnab read 22 frame(s) for this capture. — INCOMPLETE: 3 frame(s) reached the parser and produced nothing, so any count in this container is a floor. — INCOMPLETE: idle compaction discarded 4 message(s) sipnab had already captured, so the trace in this container may be shorter than the call was. Raise [limits] keep_messages_per_idle_dialog to hold more. No capture-level analysis was supplied for this export, so nothing here rules out a blind spot.",
    "sip_discarded_by_port_gate": 0,
    "sip_discarded_by_websocket_gate": 0,
    "sipnab_version": "0.5.124",
    "undecodable_frames": 3
  }
}
```

Elided at the `…` only. The fixed preamble is identical to the clean run's.

Read the shape rather than the wording.

- Every clause is a **measurement** of this run.
- None of them says the call was short, silent or broken.
  None of that follows from a capture that missed something.
- `messages_evicted:
  4` and the sentence naming it move together. So a consumer that reads fields
  reaches the same verdict as one that reads prose.

Note the last clause in both runs: no capture analysis reached this export, so
the note says so.

- "Nobody checked" and "checked and found nothing" are different answers.
- The container keeps them apart:
  - an analysis that ranked nothing emits `blind_spots: []`,
  - an export that skipped the analysis omits the field entirely.

### When the call had not ended

`call_ended` is `true` when sipnab had seen the call's closing message before it wrote the container.
That message is the BYE, CANCEL or final failure response that closes the call.

It is `false` for:

- a call still running at the end of a `-I` capture,
- a call a live export wrote after 120 seconds with no SIP and no RTP.

When it is `false`, the note adds this sentence:

```text
The call had not ended when this container was written: sipnab had seen no BYE, CANCEL or final failure for it, so the trace and any media end where this container was written, not where the call ended.
```

This is a statement about the call, not about the capture.

- So it is not an `INCOMPLETE` clause. It adds no entry to the omission rows.
- Every message sipnab held can be in the container while the call continued after sipnab
  wrote it.
- The field is always present, including as `true`.

### When a container is missing on purpose

Two of the fields in that block report a **decision** rather than a capture
fault. The note says so in words.

- Every other clause describes something the run failed to see.
- These two describe something an operator chose.
- A reader who cannot tell them apart goes looking for a fault that does not exist.

| Field | What it means |
|---|---|
| `gate_closed_during_run` | An operator stopped this run writing content partway through, over `POST /v1/persistence`. Containers are absent on one side of a hole this capture does not otherwise record. |
| `dialogs_suppressed_by_deny` | How many dialogs carried the `--content-deny-header` name and produced no container. |

`--content-deny-header` suppresses the whole dialog, not merely its content.

- The default is the conservative reading: a denied dialog leaves this process
  entirely.
  - The REST route `GET /v1/dialogs/{call_id}/vcon` answers `403` for it.
  - MCP `export_vcon` refuses it by `call_id`.
    It leaves it out of a filtered export, counting it in `withheld_by_deny`.
- `--content-deny-tombstone` makes the narrower reading available.
  - That is an identity-only container carrying a `redacted` object
    ([section 4.1.8 of the core draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.1.8)).
  - It has no message trace, no media and no bodies.
  - The trade is explicit, because a tombstone reveals that the call existed.
  - Leave it off when the header means "this call must leave no trace".

Both are always present, including as `false` and `0`.

- A missing key and "nothing happened" are the same fact here.
- There is no reason to make a consumer distinguish them.

The absence is what makes them necessary.

- A container written after recording stopped looks exactly like one from a run where those calls never happened.
  - So a reader comparing the set against a switch's records concludes sipnab missed
    them.
- The same goes for a deny flag. The containers that DID get written read
  as the complete set for their predicate.
- Neither fact survives in the capture itself. So the container carries it.

Suppression narrows and never widens.

- A header asking sipnab to RECORD is an assertion by whoever sent the request.
- This tool refuses that class of claim.
  - There is no permit flag.
  - No REST call can enable persistence a command line did not authorize.
- See [`docs/rest-api.md`](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/docs/rest-api.md)
  for the runtime gate.

## Someone handed you a sipnab vCon — what may you conclude?

Read the container as evidence from an instrument. Do not read it as a record from a
participant.

| What you see | What it licenses you to say | What it does not |
|---|---|---|
| `parties[].sip` | the `From` or `To` header carried this URI | that anyone with that URI took part |
| `parties[].sip_display_name` | the sender wrote this string in its header | that this names a person |
| `parties[].sip_user_agent` and `parties[].sip_contact` | a message this party sent carried the `User-Agent` or `Server` and `Contact` header: for the caller, the opening request; for the callee, a response from 101 to 699 carrying the dialog's remote `To` tag, or a request carrying it as the `From` tag. A proxy's `100 Trying` and any response without that tag are never read for the callee | that the software named is what the party runs |
| `validation: "none"` on every party | nobody checked anything about this party | that a check failed — the field never carries another value |
| a `role: "observer"` party | this container came from a tap | that the tap was in the media path |
| `attachments[].party` | the observer contributed this document | that a participant did |
| the message trace | these messages reached sipnab's parser | that they are all the messages |
| `analysis[0].body` | sipnab's diagnosis of what it held | a diagnosis of the call |
| `analysis[0].body.media_quality` | each RTP stream's MOS and R-factor, computed from the packets sipnab read, with `mos_grounded` saying whether the MOS rests on a published impairment value | that a listener heard that quality |
| an absent field | the capture did not carry it | that the call lacked it |
| a `dialog[]` object with no media fields | this export carries no media | that the call had none |
| `parties` on a `recording` with a `body` | the stream on each channel came from the address and port the named party advertised in its own SDP | that the party spoke, or that the channel holds only that party's audio |
| a `recording` with a `body` and no `parties` | at least one channel came from an address and port no party advertised in its SDP, such as a media relay's | that nobody was on that channel |

Three rules follow from that table.

**A missing thing is a missing observation.**

- Every absence in a sipnab vCon describes the capture. It never describes the conversation.
- That distinction is the whole reason the completeness caveat exists.
- A consumer that collapses it turns a configuration choice on a capture host into a claim about somebody's
  call.

**An unsigned container attributes nothing.** Trust it exactly as much as you
trust whoever handed it to you.

- sipnab signs an encrypted container with the key
  and certificate its operator configured.
- The signature says which operator's sipnab wrote those bytes.
- The container inside still says that sipnab observed the call and recorded nothing.

**Two containers about one call do not merge themselves.**

- sipnab writes the parties of the dialog it observed. It infers none.
- One tap on a proxied call sees two legs of one conversation, or one leg of three.
- A second tap that saw the other leg writes its own container.
- Reconciling them belongs to the consumer. The consumer is the only one holding both.

## What sipnab refuses to put in a container

Each refusal has an argument behind it in
[the design decision](https://github.com/NormB/sipnab/blob/main/docs/design/vcon.md). The one-line version:

| Refused | Why |
|---|---|
| a JWS signature on an unsigned container | a signature over an observation verifies as a signature over a recording, so sipnab signs only as the inner layer of an encrypted container you configure, with your key ([Encrypt what a rule writes](#encrypt-what-a-rule-writes)) |
| consent attachments | sipnab obtained no consent, and an empty consent field reads as "none recorded" |
| lawful-basis attachments of its own | the same, with a named regulatory reader on the other end. sipnab carries one only from an enrichment service with `lawful_basis = true`, and records that service as its source |
| a party `name` **that sipnab vouches for** | `From` and `To` are the caller's claim about the caller, trivially spoofed |
| hosted artefacts by `url`, other than audio the operator serves | sipnab hosts nothing, so it cannot promise where a file lives. The one `url` it writes is a rule's `audio = "url"` recording, under the `audio_url_base` the operator's storage serves |

**sipnab EMITS a party `name` when the wire carried one.**

- This page previously said the Rust type has no `name` field. That was wrong.
- `Party::name` exists. It carries the display name from `From` or `To`.
- It sits alongside `sip_display_name`, never instead of it.
- It travels under the declared key. So a generic vCon
  reader shows a named party rather than an anonymous one.

What sipnab refuses is not the field but the *claim*.

- `validation` is unconditionally `"none"`.
- That says a header asserted this name and nobody checked it.

**Treat it as personal data.**

- A display name is the caller's own words about who they are.
- A container is a thing operators forward.
- If you are writing a redaction step, key it on `name` AND `sip_display_name`.
- An earlier version of this page would have led you to redact only the second.

### The message trace carries the headers, and strips the credentials

Each message in the `sip-message-trace` attachment carries a `headers` object.

- It holds the header name, and an array of its values.
- So a repeated `Via` or `Record-Route` keeps the path the message actually took.

Four headers never travel:

- `Authorization`,
- `Proxy-Authorization`,
- `WWW-Authenticate`,
- `Proxy-Authenticate`.

A digest challenge and its response are credential material. A container is a publication surface.

That filter is worth one honest sentence:

- Until 0.5.125, it did nothing. The trace carried no raw headers for it to find.
- The test guarding it passed for that reason, not because the filter worked.
- Headers, and the filter that makes them safe to publish, landed together, deliberately.
- The same test now fails if anyone drops either half.

Everything else on the wire is in the container.

- Decide whether that is acceptable for your traffic before you hand one to anybody.
- `P-Asserted-Identity`, `Diversion`, `Remote-Party-ID` and any custom header your platform sets all
  travel, exactly as the endpoint wrote them.

### One thing sipnab does supply, narrowly: `tel`

A conserver indexes parties by `tel`, `mailto` and `name`, and by nothing else.

- So a consumer can retrieve a container carrying none of the three by its UUID
  and by nothing else.
- A party search never surfaces it.
- An operator who knows only the phone number cannot find the capture.

`tel` is the only one of the three sipnab can supply from evidence.

- It supplies it only when the SIP user part is unambiguously a telephone number.
  That means `+` followed by digits, an [RFC 3966](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3966.html) global number.
- Everything else gets nothing, including bare digit runs.
  - `1001` is an extension.
  - Indexing it as a telephone number would put a wrong answer in a search index rather than no
    answer.
- The observer party never carries one at all.

### The tags that tell forked legs apart

The dialog object carries `sip_from_tag` and `sip_to_tag` when the capture
observed them.

- A Call-ID alone cannot distinguish one leg of a forked INVITE
  from another. Every fork shares it.
- So a consumer correlating legs across nodes needs the tags.

`sip_to_tag` is the `To` tag of the response that established the dialog. That is:

- a 2xx answer to the opening request,
- or, when the capture holds none, a 101-199 response to it.

sipnab falls back to a tag from a response that establishes no dialog, such as a `401` or `407` challenge.

- It does this only when the capture holds neither.
- An answer under another tag replaces it.
- [RFC 3261 section 12.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3261#section-12.1)
  is the rule.

`sip_to_tag` is absent when no message carried a `To` tag. That
is itself a signal: nothing established a dialog.

## Analyze a stored vCon

`-I` reads a vCon container the way it reads a capture.

- It reads a file, a directory of them, or a glob.
- It reads them alone or beside pcap files.
- Each SIP message the container stores is rebuilt and analyzed by the same code that analyzes
  packets.
- So all of these work on it:
  - the dialog list,
  - the ladder,
  - `--report`, `--analyze`, `--json`, `--json-dialogs`,
  - the TUI.
- The MCP tool [`analyze_vcon`](@/docs/mcp-tools-vcon.md#analyze-vcon) and
  [`POST /v1/vcon/analyze`](@/docs/api.md#post-v1-vcon-analyze) do the same for a
  container handed over inline.

### Have a container

Any container with SIP in it works. This writes one from the committed sample
capture:

```sh
sipnab -N -I sip-rtp-g711.pcap --export-vcon 1-1966@10.0.2.20 --vcon-out call.vcon.json --node-name tap-a --no-cli-print --quiet
```

It prints nothing and exits 0. It leaves `call.vcon.json` beside the capture.

### Analyze it

```sh
sipnab -N -I call.vcon.json --analyze --no-cli-print --quiet
```

```text
Capture analysis: 1 finding(s) across 1 dialog(s), 0 stream(s), 6 frame(s) read.

THIS ANALYSIS IS INCOMPLETE — sipnab did not read all of this capture. The findings below describe what it UNDERSTOOD, so their counts are floors and the ABSENCE of a finding is not evidence that the problem is absent. The blind finding(s) are listed first.

1. [BLIND] Rebuilt from a stored vCon — 1 container(s)
   These dialogs were rebuilt from stored vCon containers, not read from packets. A vCon holds no RTP, so no media statistic here was computed, and whatever its producer did not store is absent. The evidence names each container, what it lacks, and the producer's own caveat.
   Evidence:
     - call.vcon.json, vcon 0158a120-0392-857f-8193-d90b5d03d6c4 | messages=6 | 6 SIP message(s) rebuilt from this container. Not recomputed or not stored: media: a vCon carries no RTP, so no stream, MOS, jitter or loss was computed from it; the producer's analysis holds 1 media_quality row(s), its own numbers, not recomputed; request-URI: not stored for 3 request(s), which carry sip:request-uri-not-stored.invalid; header order: the trace keys headers by name, so their order across names is the container's, not the wire's, and headers the producer did not store (credential headers, when sipnab produced it) are absent. The producer's caveat: Produced by sipnab 0.5.208 on node tap-a. sipnab OBSERVED this dialog and took no part in it: the parties below are what the From and To headers said, not identities anyone established, and nothing here is signed. No media is in this container because this run decoded none for the dialog; the capture_completeness media_note says what was measured. That is a statement about what this run kept, not a finding that the call was silent. sipnab read 852 frame(s) for this capture. No omissions recorded: every message sipnab held for this dialog is in this container. A capture-level analysis ran and ranked no blind spots.
```

The first finding is `rebuilt_from_vcon`. It is a `blind` finding.

- The analysis is of what the container stored.
- The finding names what that leaves out.
- Then it quotes the producer's own caveat.

Every message says where it came from:

```sh
sipnab -N -I call.vcon.json --json --quiet | head -1 | jq '{timestamp, src, dst, transport, method, input_origin}'
```

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2016-11-26T14:52:59.666393+00:00",
  "src": "10.0.2.20",
  "dst": "10.0.2.15",
  "transport": "UDP",
  "method": "INVITE",
  "input_origin": "vcon"
}
```

The `-N` summary line and the TUI's raw message view mark the same messages
`origin=vcon`.

### A directory of them

Write one container per INVITE dialog into `stored`. It prints
`Wrote 2 vCon container(s) to 'stored'.`

```sh
sipnab -N -I sip-rtp-g711.pcap --export-vcon-when 'method == "INVITE"' --export-vcon-dir stored --node-name tap-a --no-cli-print --quiet
```

Add a container that stores no SIP at all:

```sh
printf '{"vcon": "0.4.0", "parties": []}\n' > stored/broken.vcon.json
```

Read the directory. sipnab names the container it cannot read, with the reason.
It reads the rest:

```sh
sipnab -N -I stored --json-dialogs --no-cli-print --quiet | jq -c '{call_id, msg_count, final_status_code, input_origin}'
```

```text
2026-10-09T15:22:57.015657Z  WARN sipnab::capture::input_set: Skipping 'stored/broken.vcon.json': not a readable capture (a vCon container with no SIP signaling sipnab can read: it has no sip-message-trace or message/sip attachment)
2026-10-09T15:22:57.017252Z  WARN sipnab::capture::input_set: -I resolved to 2 capture file(s), 1 file(s) that are not readable captures
{"call_id":"1-1966@10.0.2.20","msg_count":6,"final_status_code":200,"input_origin":"vcon"}
{"call_id":"1-1968@10.0.2.20","msg_count":4,"final_status_code":200,"input_origin":"vcon"}
```

A container named directly with `-I` that sipnab cannot read stops the run
instead, with the same reason. A file you named is one you expected
sipnab to read.

### Read many containers at once

`--report` over a directory of containers prints one row per container after
the dialog table. Each row says whether sipnab read the container or skipped
it, and then the totals:

```sh
sipnab -N -I stored --report --no-cli-print --quiet
```

```text
Call-ID                          From           To             State        Code   Duration   Msgs   PDD      Tags
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1-1966@10.0.2.20                 sipp           test           Completed    200    8s         6      -        -
1-1968@10.0.2.20                 sipp           test           InCall       200    0s         4      -        -

vCon containers:
Status                     Form       Findings  Calls  Duration  Disposition              UUID                                  File
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
read                       unsigned   0         1      8s        Completed 1              0158a120-0392-8a4b-8522-17eac0c8ec4b  stored/1-1966_10.0.2.20-1cc03f180ff8a774.vcon.json
read                       unsigned   0         1      0s        InCall 1                 0158a120-253e-8af9-a5b5-76781dbeae49  stored/1-1968_10.0.2.20-cdd887baa4507e9a.vcon.json
skipped: no_sip_signaling  unsigned   1         0      0s        -                        -                                     stored/broken.vcon.json

Totals: 3 container(s): 2 read, 1 skipped
Skipped by reason: no_sip_signaling 1
Failed validation: 1 container(s)
Calls: 2 (Completed 1, InCall 1)
Total duration: 8s

Skipped:
  stored/broken.vcon.json: a vCon container with no SIP signaling sipnab can read: it has no sip-message-trace or message/sip attachment
```

The `Skipping` warnings print on standard error as before. `--quiet` hides
them, and the report keeps each reason.

The columns:

- **Status.** `read`, or `skipped:` and the reason in one word:
  - `no_key`: the container is in the encrypted form and the run has no `--vcon-key`.
    Give the flag to read it.
  - `no_sip_signaling`: the container stores no SIP message sipnab can
    rebuild.
  - `not_json`: the file starts with `{` and is not JSON.
  - `not_a_vcon`: the JSON is not a vCon.
  - `not_opened`: a signed or encrypted layer did not open, for a reason
    other than a missing key.
  - `unsupported_critical`: `critical` lists an extension sipnab does not
    support.
  - `unreadable`: sipnab cannot read the file, or the file is over 64 MiB.
- **Form.** The outermost form the file arrived in: `unsigned`, `signed`,
  `encrypted` or `gzip`, or `unknown` for bytes that are not a JSON object.
- **Findings.** How many places the container disagrees with the vendored
  draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04 schema. `-` means the schema check did not
  run, because the file did not open or is not JSON.
- **Calls.** The calls rebuilt from the container, by Call-ID.
- **Duration.** Those calls' durations added up, each as the dialog table's
  Duration column computes it.
- **Disposition.** Those calls counted by state, the word the dialog table's
  State column prints.
- **UUID** and **File.** The container's `uuid`, and the file.

The totals add up the rows. A call that two containers both hold counts once
in the totals and once in each of their rows. `Failed validation` counts the
containers with at least one schema finding, read or skipped.

The section prints only when the run met a container. A report over a
capture prints what it printed before. `--filter` does not narrow it: a container is an input,
like a capture file.

When sipnab skips every file in the directory, for example a directory that
holds only encrypted containers and the run has no `--vcon-key`, the run
still fails. It prints `no readable capture files` on standard error and
exits 1, as it does without `--report`. Before it exits, `--report` prints
the `vCon containers:` section, with no dialog table, so each container
still has its row, the totals and the reason in full. With `--json` or
`--json-pretty`, it prints the `sipnab_vcon_containers` object in place of
the section. Without `--report`, or when the directory holds no vCon
container, the run prints nothing on standard output.

With `--json` or `--json-pretty`, the same rows and totals come as one JSON
object under the key `sipnab_vcon_containers`, in place of the text section.
The dialog table stays text:

```sh
sipnab -N -I stored --report --json --no-cli-print --quiet | grep sipnab_vcon_containers | jq '.sipnab_vcon_containers.totals'
```

```json
{
  "calls": 2,
  "containers": 3,
  "dispositions": {
    "Completed": 1,
    "InCall": 1
  },
  "duration_secs": 8,
  "failed_validation": 1,
  "read": 2,
  "skipped": 1,
  "skipped_by_reason": {
    "no_sip_signaling": 1
  }
}
```

Each row of `containers` carries `status`, `file`, `uuid`, `form`,
`validation_findings` (null where the text prints `-`), `calls_rebuilt`,
`call_ids`, `dispositions` and `duration_secs`. A skipped row also carries
`skip_reason` and `skip_detail`, the reason in full.

The MCP tool [`vcon_directory_report`](@/docs/mcp-tools-vcon.md#vcon-directory-report)
answers the same report for a directory of `--mcp-file-root`, with the rows
paged.

### A signed, encrypted or compressed container

A vCon arrives in one of three JSON forms, and a producer may compress any of them
([draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04 section 5.4](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-5.4)).
Every reader opens each one with the same step: `-I`, `analyze_vcon`,
`validate_vcon`, `POST /v1/vcon/analyze` and `POST /v1/vcon/validate`.

- The gzip format ([section 6.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-6.2)):
  - sipnab knows it by the gzip magic bytes `1f 8b`, under any file name.
  - It inflates it, up to 64 MiB, and reads the form inside.
  - A gzip-compressed capture inflates to a capture and stays a capture.
- The signed form ([section 5.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-5.2)):
  - sipnab verifies the signature against the first certificate in `x5c`.
  - It refuses a container whose signature does not verify.
  - It needs no key.
- The encrypted form ([section 5.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-5.3)):
  - sipnab decrypts it with the private key `--vcon-key` names, or
    `[vcon_input] key`. The key file must be readable by its owner only.
  - It then verifies the signed form inside. It refuses an encrypted container
    that does not hold the signed form.
  - Without a key it refuses the container and names the flag. It never
    analyzes the encrypted JSON as a container with no SIP.

So sipnab reads its own encrypted output back. This `sipnab.toml` writes the
two INVITE dialogs of the sample capture encrypted and gzip compressed, as
[Encrypt what a rule writes](#encrypt-what-a-rule-writes) describes.
`recipient.key` is the private key of `recipient.crt`, mode `0600`:

```toml
[[vcon.rule]]
name = "sealed"
when = "method == \"INVITE\""
dir = "sealed"
encrypt_to = "recipient.crt"
sign_key = "signer.key"
sign_cert = "signer-chain.pem"
compress = "gzip"
```

```sh
# Run all of these, in order.
sipnab -N -I sip-rtp-g711.pcap --config sipnab.toml --no-cli-print --quiet
sipnab -N -I sealed --vcon-key recipient.key --json-dialogs --no-cli-print --quiet | jq -c '{call_id, msg_count, input_origin}'
```

```text
[[vcon.rule]] 'sealed': Wrote 2 vCon container(s) to 'sealed'.
{"call_id":"1-1966@10.0.2.20","msg_count":6,"input_origin":"vcon"}
{"call_id":"1-1968@10.0.2.20","msg_count":4,"input_origin":"vcon"}
```

Without `--vcon-key`, a container named with `-I` stops the run with exit 1:

```text
cannot open the vCon container: the container is encrypted (draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04 section 5.3), and no decryption key was given: give --vcon-key, or [vcon_input] key in the config file
```

A gzip format vCon reads like any other:

```sh
# Run all of these, in order.
gzip -k call.vcon.json
sipnab -N -I call.vcon.json.gz --json-dialogs --no-cli-print --quiet | jq -c '{call_id, msg_count}'
```

```text
{"call_id":"1-1966@10.0.2.20","msg_count":6}
```

The `rebuilt_from_vcon` finding names each layer sipnab opened, and who signed it:

```text
Opened from: encrypted form, decrypted; signed form, verified, signer SHA-256 4A:27:CF:...
```

Two settings check who signed it, as the fetcher's do
([Check who signed it](#check-who-signed-it)):

- `--vcon-signer-ca <FILE|system>` (`[vcon_input] signer_ca`): the signing
  certificate must chain to a CA in the file, every certificate within its
  validity period.
- `--vcon-signer-sha256 <HEX>` (`[vcon_input] signer_sha256`): the signing
  certificate must have this fingerprint.
- With either set, sipnab refuses an unsigned container: it has no signer to
  check.

The MCP and REST readers:

- `analyze_vcon` takes a signed or encrypted container as `container`, and
  any form, the gzip format included, as `container_base64`.
- `POST /v1/vcon/analyze` and `POST /v1/vcon/validate` take a JSON body with
  `Content-Type: application/json`, `application/vcon` or
  `application/vcon+json`, and a gzip format body with
  `Content-Type: application/vcon+gzip`.
- `validate_vcon` and `POST /v1/vcon/validate` validate the unsigned vCon
  inside.
- A container that does not open is a `verdict: unreadable` answer from the
  analyze tool and route. The validate tool and route refuse it; the route
  answers `422`.
- They read with the server's `--vcon-key`, `--vcon-signer-ca` and
  `--vcon-signer-sha256`.

### A container listing an extension sipnab does not support is not read

A container's `critical` parameter lists the extensions a reader must support
to interpret it.

- [Section 4.1.4 of draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.1.4)
  says a reader that does not support one "MUST NOT attempt to process or
  operate on the vCon, except to reject it or report unsupported content".
- sipnab supports the two extensions its own containers declare, `sip-signaling` and `CC`.
- sipnab skips a container whose `critical` lists anything else, as it skips a
  container without readable SIP. The reason names each unsupported extension.
- `analyze_vcon` and `POST /v1/vcon/analyze` answer `verdict: unreadable` with
  that reason. They run no schema check.
- `validate_vcon` and `POST /v1/vcon/validate` refuse the container.

### A container the schema refuses is still read

What sipnab skips is a container whose SIP it cannot read.

- Some containers disagree with the vendored draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04 schema but store
  readable SIP. Such a container still reads.
- sipnab reports the finding with it.
- The common case is a container that went through vcon.store. vcon.store hands `extensions` back as an
  object rather than the array the schema requires:

```sh
jq '.extensions = {"sip-signaling": true, "CC": true}' call.vcon.json > store-shape.vcon.json
```

```sh
sipnab -N -I store-shape.vcon.json --json-dialogs --no-cli-print --quiet | jq -c '{call_id, msg_count, input_origin}'
```

```text
2026-10-09T15:22:57.067344Z  WARN sipnab::capture::file: 'store-shape.vcon.json' fails the draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04 schema (/extensions (type): expected type "array", found object); its SIP is read regardless, and the analysis carries the finding(s)
{"call_id":"1-1966@10.0.2.20","msg_count":6,"input_origin":"vcon"}
```

The `rebuilt_from_vcon` finding in `--analyze` carries the same schema finding
for that container. The MCP tool and the REST route list it in
`schema_findings`.

### What sipnab reads, and what cannot come back

- **Two stored forms.**
  - The first is the `sip-message-trace` attachment sipnab writes, and
    the trace form of draft-howe-vcon-sip-signaling-00 it extends.
    These give each message its time, addresses, ports and transport.
  - The second is `message/sip` attachments, the draft's other form.
    - They carry each message whole, timed by the attachment's `start`.
    - That form stores no addressing. So those messages carry
      `0.0.0.0:0`, and the finding says so.
  - A container with neither form holds nothing to analyze.
    An example is the recording-only example in core-04 Appendix A.
    sipnab skips it with that reason.
- **Detection is by content.**
  - sipnab reads a file whose first character other
    than whitespace is `{` as a container, whatever its name.
  - Some JSON objects have none of the members a vCon has (`vcon`, `uuid`, `created_at`, `parties`,
    `dialog`, `analysis`, `attachments`). Such an object is not one. sipnab skips it with
    that reason.
  - `extensions` counts in either form, the core-04 array or the
    vcon.store object.
- **sipnab skips unreadable SIP, not a schema finding.**
  - It skips a container with no `sip-message-trace` or `message/sip` attachment, naming the reason.
  - It also skips a container whose attachments
    hold no message it can rebuild, naming the reason.
  - It reads a container that fails the schema and stores readable SIP. It reports the finding.
- **One container is at most 64 MiB.**
  - sipnab reads a container whole to validate it.
  - So it refuses a file larger than `MAX_CONTAINER_BYTES`
    (67,108,864 bytes) without reading it. It names the size and the limit.
  - As with any container it cannot read, sipnab skips it in a directory or a glob.
    It stops the run when you name it directly.
  - A container carrying inline audio within
    the 5 MiB default budget is far below the limit.
- **No media.**
  - A vCon stores no RTP. So sipnab computes no stream, MOS,
    jitter or loss from it.
  - It reports no media fault for a call that had none
    to measure.
  - `analyze_vcon` and `POST /v1/vcon/analyze` return the producer's
    own `media_quality` numbers verbatim, as its numbers.
- **No request-URI.** The trace stores the method, not the request line.
  - So a rebuilt request carries `sip:request-uri-not-stored.invalid`.
  - That is a name in the reserved `.invalid` domain.
- **Some things do not come back:**
  - header order across names,
  - bodies other than SDP,
  - headers the producer did not store (sipnab removes credential headers).
  - `Content-Length` states the body the container holds.
- **No frame pointers.** A rebuilt message was never a frame anyone can read
  again. So it carries none.
- **`--redact`ed containers** read back with their pseudonyms. Nothing can
  recover the originals from them.
- **Not with `--cores` or a BPF filter.**
  - `--cores` shards captured frames. A BPF filter selects them.
  - A container holds neither. So sipnab refuses both, with the reason.
  - Select dialogs with `--filter` instead.
- **sipnab sends nothing anywhere.** The addresses in a container are a record
  of a finished call. So sipnab never transmits a response to them.

## The uuid under a domain

By default sipnab keys a container's uuid on the node, the dialog and the capture
(see [What this does not do](#what-this-does-not-do)). That departs from
[draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04 section 4.1.2](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-4.1.2),
which says:

<!-- vale Google.Passive = NO -->
> The value of the string SHOULD be generated using the version 8 UUID
> defined in [UUID] which is generated identically to a version 7 UUID
> with the exception that:
>
> - rand_b/custom_c is generated from the high 62 bits of the SHA-1
>   hash of the FQHN string
> - the variant and version fields are set as described for version 8
>   UUID
>
> The DNS name string used in generating the uuid value SHOULD be the
> same FQHN, or a subdomain to allow for more distributed generation of
> UUIDs, as would used in the signing certificate as they are the same
> domains of uniqueness.
<!-- vale Google.Passive = YES -->

`[vcon] uuid_domain` writes that form:

```toml
[vcon]
uuid_domain = "node1.pbx.example.com"
```

Every container uuid the process writes then has this layout. That covers the
batch export, `GET /v1/dialogs/{id}/vcon`, MCP `export_vcon` and the
related-legs attachment.

| Bits | Field ([RFC 9562 section 5.7](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9562.html#section-5.7)) | What sipnab puts there |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 0-47 | `unix_ts_ms` | The call's first observed message, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. The same as the default |
| 48-51 | `ver` | `8` |
| 52-63 | `rand_a` | 12 bits seeded from SHA-256 over the Call-ID and the capture identity, the same seed as the default. See below for when it is not |
| 64-65 | `var` | `10` |
| 66-127 | `rand_b` | The high 62 bits of SHA-1 over the domain. sipnab hashes the name in lower case, without a trailing dot |

sipnab refuses at startup, with exit code 1 and a message naming
`[vcon] uuid_domain`, a value that is not a host name of two or more labels.
Each label must be 1 to 63 ASCII letters, digits or hyphens, and must not start or end
with a hyphen. The whole name is at most 253 characters. Write an
internationalized name in its `xn--` form. sipnab also refuses an IPv4
address. See [the error reference](@/docs/errors.md).

**What the layout leaves for uniqueness.** Section 4.1.2 also says "The UUID
value MUST be globally unique". Under one domain, the timestamp and the 62
domain bits are the same for every call that starts in the same millisecond.
Only `rand_a`'s 12 bits separate those calls: 4096 values per millisecond per
domain.

- Seeded from the dialog alone, two calls in one millisecond would share a uuid
  once in 4096 pairs. So sipnab keeps a table of the values it has given out.
  A call whose seed picks a value already given in that millisecond takes the
  next free one.
- The table is per process. A second sipnab process, or a second node, under
  the same domain cannot see it. Give each node its own subdomain, as the
  draft's "or a subdomain to allow for more distributed generation of UUIDs"
  allows.
- The table holds at most 1,048,576 uuids. Past that it drops its oldest
  milliseconds, and sipnab seeds a call from one of them afresh.
- When calls hold all 4096 values of a millisecond, the next call repeats a
  uuid. The layout has no room to prevent that.

**What stays deterministic.** The seed is a function of the dialog and the
capture. So re-exporting one call, or running the same capture again, writes
the same uuid. The exception is a call that met a seed collision in its
millisecond: its value depends on which of the two calls sipnab minted first.

**Later versions.** A `sealed_updates = "new-uuid"` rule's version *n* keeps the
first version's timestamp and the domain's 62 bits. sipnab seeds its `rand_a`
from SHA-256 over `amended`, the first uuid and *n*, through the same table. So
two versions of one call differ in those 12 bits alone.

**Not done: the domain from `sign_cert`.** The draft asks for the name "as
would used in the signing certificate". sipnab does not read it from
`sign_cert`. Set `uuid_domain` to the DNS name in that certificate, or to a
subdomain of it.

## What this does not do

Stated here rather than discovered later.

- **It does not host audio.**
  - When the run retained the RTP payload, the container carries the audio INLINE.
    It is a `recording` Dialog Object with a `sha512-` content hash.
  - A rule with `audio = "url"` instead writes the audio file beside the container.
    It names the file by a `url` under the rule's `audio_url_base`, with the
    `content_hash` of the file and no body.
  - The operator's storage serves that URL. sipnab does not check that it does.
  - A `--redact` export never names a `url`.
  - When the run retained no audio, the container says so in words and carries none.

  Audio over the inline budget draws an out-loud refusal rather than a silent truncation.

  - `--vcon-max-inline-media` sets that budget in MiB. It defaults to 5.
  - That figure comes from a measurement against a real vCon store. The store:
    - answered `204` for a container of roughly 12 MB,
    - wrote it to its database,
    - had its own file spool refuse the payload,
    - and neither side reported the partial write.
  - `0` refuses every inline body without turning the exporter off.

  sipnab retains whole calls. So a call's audio grows with its length.

  - A two-way 20 ms G.711 call exports as 8 kHz stereo. That is 32,000 bytes of WAV a
    second.
  - It fits the 5 MiB default for up to 122 seconds.
  - At 123 seconds, the container carries the refusal instead.
  - As Ogg Opus (`audio_format = "opus"`) the same call fits for up to 643 seconds. See [Audio as Ogg Opus](#audio-as-ogg-opus).
  - Raise `--vcon-max-inline-media` to what the store you send to accepts.
    Or write the WAV beside the container with the `export_audio` MCP tool.

  A `--redact` export carries no audio at all.

  - Redaction deletes audio rather than replacing it with a token.
  - Its Dialog Object is the signaling one, typed by the rule above.
  - `capture_completeness.media` says `withheld-by-redaction`.

  Every door (batch export, REST and MCP) reads the one value.
  So the same call cannot come back carrying
  audio through one and a refusal through another.
- **It ties the legs of a B2BUA call together only by its correlation.**
  - With `grouping = "leg"`, the default, two Call-IDs produce two containers.
    Each names the other in its `sipnab-related-legs` attachment, with the
    strategy that tied them.
  - With `grouping = "call"` one container holds every leg the rule selects.
  - A tie that is a timing guess carries `identifier_match: false`. A busy
    server can get it wrong.
  - See [Calls through a PBX or a B2BUA](#calls-through-a-pbx-or-a-b2bua).
- **It does not write a `.vconz` bundle.**
  - draft-miller-vcon-zip-bundle-00 names each external file by its `content_hash`, with an extension from the `mediatype`.
  - For an encrypted recording that rule gives the ciphertext an `.ogg` or `.wav` extension.
  - For an encrypted vCon the draft says both that a bundle creator MUST NOT decrypt and that it SHOULD decrypt when it holds the keys.
  - The draft expired on May 10, 2026.
- **It does not assemble a call across hops.** One container describes one
  observed dialog from one capture.
- **It does not deduplicate across taps.**
  - Two sipnab boxes that saw the same dialog mint different uuids.
  - The uuid mixes in the node and the capture identity along with the Call-ID.
- **Its uuid is a function of the dialog, the node and the capture, not a
  random value.**
  - The 48-bit timestamp is the dialog's first observed message.
  - The other 74 bits are digests. `rand_a` (12 bits) digests the Call-ID and
    the capture identity. `rand_b` (62 bits) digests the node name, the Call-ID
    and the capture identity.
  - Two dialogs that opened in the same millisecond on one node differ in those 74 bits.
  - Re-exporting one dialog from one capture yields the same uuid. So
    deduplication on `uuid` is safe for re-exports. That is what it exists for.
  - Until 0.5.125 `rand_b` digested the node alone. That left 12 bits to
    separate such dialogs.
  - `[vcon] uuid_domain` replaces `rand_b` with the high 62 bits of SHA-1 over
    a host name, the form section 4.1.2 asks for. See
    [The uuid under a domain](#the-uuid-under-a-domain).
- **It does not store anything.** sipnab writes a container and forgets it.
  There is no vCon store, no index, no retention.
